title: Transcript input sets are rectangles
statement: Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party protocol with input types $X$ and $Y$ and output type $\alpha$, and let $t$ be a transcript of $p$. The set of input pairs that follow the path recorded by $t$ is a rectangle: there are sets $A\subseteq X$ and $B\subseteq Y$ such that this input set is $A\times B$.
hypotheses_covered: A deterministic protocol over input types $X$ and $Y$ with output type $\alpha$
replaced:
Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol over input types $X$ (Alice)
and $Y$ (Bob) with output type $\alpha$, and let $t$ be a syntactic transcript of $p$.
Then the input set of $t$ — the set of all input pairs $(x, y) \in X \times Y$ whose
execution of $p$ follows exactly the path recorded by $t$ — is a rectangle: there exist
$A \subseteq X$ and $B \subseteq Y$ such that this set equals $A \times B$.
